title: Agentic Systems Architect

research_window.rule: Postings dated on or after the cutoff count toward frequency. Older postings are retained as corroborating evidence but excluded from the in-window count.

notes: Second cycle. The 2026-06-14 seed (Imagine Learning) was sharpened by 25+ additional Agentic AI/Systems Architect postings from Mar-Jun 2026. Result: the existing 10-module spine (mod-301..mod-310) and the three projects continue to cover every requirement that crosses the 0.30 frequency threshold. No new modules, exercises, or projects are warranted this cycle. See JOB_REQUIREMENTS.md for the human-readable mapping and rationale. Frequency counts in this file are computed against the 22 in-window postings only.
summary: The market for 'Agentic Systems Architect' has matured into a recognizable archetype with three sub-flavors: (a) the consulting/SI architect (Cognizant, Capgemini, Infosys, EY, Guidehouse, NTT DATA, WGA, dentsu, Granicus) who scopes/architects agentic platforms for clients; (b) the enterprise-platform architect (84.51°/Kroger, UnitedHealth, Acquia, Experian, Vertex, Apollo, Zoom, HERE Technologies) who owns the internal agent reference architecture, registry, observability and governance; and (c) the security/governance-leaning architect (Zscaler, Imagine Learning) focused on secure agent runtimes, MCP/tool registries, OAuth/RBAC, prompt-injection defense. All three flavors converge on the same core skill set: (i) multi-agent orchestration architecture with frameworks (LangGraph/CrewAI/AutoGen/Semantic Kernel) and protocols (MCP/A2A); (ii) memory/context engineering and RAG; (iii) evaluation harnesses (offline + online, trajectory + final-state); (iv) observability/tracing (OTel GenAI, LangFuse/LangSmith/Arize); (v) secure agent execution (OAuth/RBAC, tool sandboxing, prompt-injection mitigation, MCP server/tool registries); (vi) governance and regulated-domain compliance (ISO/IEC 42001, FERPA/COPPA/HIPAA/FedRAMP-relevant patterns); (vii) durable execution and HITL; (viii) cost/latency economics; (ix) pre-sales / executive scoping & adoption. Every one of these is already a module in the existing curriculum.

requirements.text: Design and evolve a plugin-based architecture (Agents, Skills, Hooks, Model Context Protocol/MCP) to extend an agentic coding tool so AI can securely interface with internal SDLC toolchains and proprietary data.
Develop and optimize production AI applications via prompt engineering, context management, and tool-use patterns.
Develop reliable tool-use patterns and context-hydration strategies giving the agent precise system access/context to execute SDLC and other autonomous tasks.
Design AI systems compliant with data privacy / regulatory requirements (FERPA, COPPA, HIPAA, FedRAMP, federal Public Trust).
Design developer-focused tooling emphasizing usability, adoption, onboarding, documentation, and continuous feedback loops.
Apply a security-first approach to local and remote agent execution: robust sandboxing, strict permission scopes, secure auth flows, OWASP LLM Top 10 / MITRE ATLAS / NIST AI RMF awareness.
Drive governance for an agentic platform: how plugins/agents/tools are evaluated, versioned, approved, monitored; align with AI governance frameworks (ISO/IEC 42001, RAI principles).
Lead estimation, scoping, and planning for AI/ML initiatives with executive and senior stakeholders; deliver via Agile/SDLC; client/pre-sales scoping where applicable.
Lead continuous improvement across system architecture and AI model integration via measurable outcomes (evaluation + observability).
8 years as Lead Software Engineer / Platform Architect / AI Engineering Lead (or graduate-equivalent shorter tracks). Postings range 7-15+ yrs.
requirements.note: Prerequisite/experience gate, not a teachable module. Recorded in PREREQUISITES.md.

requirements.text: Proven experience building AI-enabled developer tooling, function-calling/tool-use pipelines, or extensible agentic platforms in production; architecting modular, extensible, scalable platforms.
Proficiency in Python and TypeScript/Node.js; modular APIs/SDKs/CLI; REST, GraphQL, event-driven architectures.
requirements.note: Track examples provided in both TS/Node and Python.

requirements.text: Working knowledge of data privacy/compliance requirements in regulated environments.
Deep understanding of secure system design: OAuth, token management, RBAC; mitigating insecure tool execution and prompt injection.
Intimate knowledge of modern SDLC and integrating with core DevOps and PM toolchains (GitHub, Confluence, Jira, CI/CD).
Model Context Protocol (MCP) integration: build/secure MCP servers, tool registries, connector patterns; previously preferred, now appears across 9/22 in-window postings.
